fieldMarks: Chunky brown grouse, 41-48 cm, heavily barred, especially on the underparts.
Short black tail visible in flight.
Male has yellow-orange neck air sacs and raised feather tufts, visible only in courtship display.
behavior: In spring, typically 8-20 males gather on 'booming grounds', often a low hill with good visibility, and display with a hollow moaning 'boom', foot-stamping and cackles.
Some birds are permanent residents; others move up to about 160 km (100 miles) between breeding and wintering areas.
Forages mostly on the ground, mainly in early morning and evening; winter diet is leaves, seeds and waste grain, summer diet adds buds, berries and insects.
habitat: Native tall-grass prairie, including prairie interspersed with agricultural fields; prime original habitat was prairie mixed with oak woodland. Nests on the ground in thick tall grass.
range: Now uncommon and localized to remaining native tall-grass prairie in the midwestern United States. The Atlantic Coast race (Heath Hen) became extinct in 1932 and the Texas coastal Attwater's race is seriously endangered.
